summary.text: A 38-year-old woman with an IVF-conceived dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy, a prior IVF twin pregnancy delivered by cesarean section nine years earlier, no previous miscarriages and no significant family history, although her sister-in-law's child has Down syndrome.

Screening at 12+4 weeks showed an absent nasal bone and nuchal translucency of 3 mm in twin II with normal findings in twin I; NIPT at 13+1 weeks indicated high risk for trisomy 21 in twin II, which amniocentesis at 16+3 weeks and QF-PCR/CMA at 20+6 weeks confirmed, while twin I had a normal male karyotype.
Serial ultrasounds showed reduced fetal movements, oligohydramnios and an absent nasal bone in twin II, including on 4D ultrasound at 31 weeks, with twin I within normal limits.

Because selective feticide was forbidden in Bosnia and Herzegovina, she was referred to the Clinical Center of Serbia, where the Ethics Committee approved it; at 33+1 weeks ultrasound-guided selective feticide of twin II with 8 mL of 7.45% KCl into the fetal heart was followed by confirmation of asystole the same day.

At 33+6 weeks, because of regular uterine contractions and obstetric indications, a cesarean section delivered a live male infant (twin I, 2,440 g, 44 cm, Apgar score 6) and a stillborn male infant (twin II, 1,900 g, 45 cm, Apgar score 0).

The maternal postoperative course was uneventful with discharge on postoperative day 11 and no adverse maternal outcomes; the surviving infant had appropriate growth and development at one-month follow-up.
